description:
## CONTEXT

The wire ships the artifact N+1 times and embeds full prompts inside retry instructions -- the mechanical cause of the 73k-207k-char envelopes observed in the field (decision record: workspace N-076; MCP state-mule report). The server already keeps reviewId-keyed state on disk; this ticket makes later hops REFERENCE it instead of re-passing it. DEPENDS ON LF1: LF1 adds artifact + changedFiles retention to `ReviewSession`, which is the missing server-side input this delta protocol needs. Land LF1 first.

## VERIFIED STATE @ a9f49dd

- The artifact is interpolated into every lens prompt via the shared preamble (shared-preamble.ts:174-179), so a large diff is duplicated across every activated lens, each stored per lens on disk (`writePrompt`, review-state.ts:268-270) and streamed whole through `lens_review_get_prompt` (get-prompt.ts:88-96).
- The complete response embeds the ENTIRE original prompt inside every `NextAction.retryPrompt`: `` `${prompt}\n\n<retry-context>...` `` (src/tools/complete.ts:273). Two retryable lenses put two full prompts (each preamble + body + artifact) into one tool result.
- The server already has reviewId-keyed prompts, promptHashes, per-lens expiry, and cached results that survive restart (review-state.ts:306-390; the in-flight index/task/prompt files at in-flight.ts:9-16). The only missing later-hop inputs are the artifact and changedFiles themselves -- supplied by LF1.
- The server advertises exactly three tools (server.ts:40-59); there is no verdict read-back (that gap is LF4, not this ticket).

## SCOPE (additive, gated on a start-time `protocol: 2` field so v1 callers are untouched)

1. Hop-1 request stays `{stage, artifact | artifactRef, changedFiles, configs}`; the response returns `{reviewId, protocolVersion, agents:[{id, model, promptHash, expiresAt}], cached}` with the artifact stored once server-side (via LF1 retention) rather than echoed in the response.
2. Hop-1b `get_prompt(reviewId, lensId)` unchanged for subagents (one prompt per subagent context, never routed through the orchestrator).
3. Hop-2+ `complete(reviewId, results:[{lensId, attempt, output}])` accepts partial batches (coordinate with LF2's per-lens acceptance); the response REPLACES `retryPrompt` (complete.ts:273) with a compact `{lensId, attempt, retryContext, expiresAt}` (~300 bytes each); the agent re-fetches the base prompt via `get_prompt` and appends `retryContext`. This bounds the complete envelope to findings + coverage.
4. Payload budgets + response envelopes sized for tool-result caps; expiry semantics for retained state reuse the 24h in-flight TTL (`DEFAULT_TTL_MS`, in-flight.ts:51); after expiry, later hops return a typed `REVIEW_EXPIRED`.
5. v1 back-compat path: when `protocol` is absent or `1`, behavior is byte-identical to today (full `retryPrompt`, inline artifact echoed exactly as now).

## OUT OF SCOPE

The artifact-retention mechanism itself (LF1 owns it); verdict read-back (LF4); coverage disclosure (LF2). This ticket is purely the delta-transport shape on top of LF1's retention.

## ACCEPTANCE

- Test: a `protocol: 2` hop-1 response for a large artifact is under a small fixed budget (e.g. < 5KB) and does not contain the artifact text.
- Test: a `protocol: 2` complete response for two retryable lenses is bounded (retryContext refs, not full prompts) and stays well under the tool-result cap; a `protocol: 1` complete still returns the full `retryPrompt` (back-compat pinned).
- Test: `get_prompt` after hop-1 returns the same prompt string it did before (identity preserved, per get-prompt.ts:24-29).
- Test: a later hop past the 24h TTL returns `REVIEW_EXPIRED`.
- Test: end to end, a `protocol: 2` review reaches the same verdict as the equivalent `protocol: 1` review over the same inputs.

## PITFALLS

- Must not land before LF1: without server-side artifact retention there is nothing to reference.
- The `retryContext` ref path changes the subagent contract (the agent must re-fetch and append) -- document it in the tool descriptions; a v1 agent handed a v2 response would otherwise lose its prompt.
- Keep the protocol flag strictly additive; a missing flag must select v1 exactly.
- Do not break the existing get-prompt invariant "retry prompts are never fetched via this tool" (get-prompt.ts:26-29): under v2, `retryContext` is appended to a freshly fetched BASE prompt, which is consistent with that invariant.

## VERIFICATION

Record envelope sizes for a 100KB-diff review under protocol 1 vs 2 at hop-1 and at a two-lens retry; assert the v2 sizes collapse into the tool-result cap while the v1 sizes reproduce the 70k+ band; confirm identical verdicts across the two protocols.

## SIZING

L. tools/start.ts, tools/complete.ts, tools/get-prompt.ts, state/review-state.ts, cache/in-flight.ts, schema params + verdict. Gated and additive but touches the whole transport. Portable enough for the lowest permitted execution tier provided LF1 has landed; the protocol-versioning branch must be specified explicitly at plan time.

Cross-link: workspace N-076. blockedBy LF1 (retention enabler).

PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS (2026-07-04, wave 3b, binding):

Adjudication of the wave-3 plan gate for T-032. One plan round was reviewed at HEAD 770cfd5 by two reviewers: codex review_plan (verdict revise, findings CF1-CF5) and an independent repo-verifying reviewer (verdict revise, findings VF1-VF7). All findings were re-derived against source at 770cfd5 during adjudication. Every ruling below is binding on the next planner; the reviewed plan's "Exact edits" and T1-T8 test list are ratified EXCEPT where amended here. The plan's verified engineering claims (retryPrompt decomposes byte-for-byte into prompt + suffix at src/tools/complete.ts:273; hop-1 already refs-not-prompts per src/tools/start.ts:87-109; protocol persistence via optional index field is strict-parse back-compatible) were independently confirmed and stand as fact.

R1 (blocker gate; resolves CF1 + VF6). Option A is ratified: T-026 lands earlier in this same wave, and T-032 builds on T-026's retained artifact. blockedBy T-026 stays until T-026's commit exists on local main; no descoped early start. SCOPE-1's "artifact stored once server-side" is delivered by T-022 (already at HEAD: StartToolOutputSchema returns {reviewId, agents, cached} with no artifact echo, start.ts:87-109) plus T-026's retention (ReviewSession.artifact/changedFiles + in-flight persistence). The plan's finding that the retry-transport core is LF1-independent (it references session.prompts, review-state.ts:52-67, never the artifact) is accepted as fact but does not override the wave ordering. The next planner MUST re-verify every line citation at the actual parent commit, since T-026 edits the same files.

R2 (v1 byte-identity, the load-bearing back-compat ruling; resolves CF2 + VF2). When `protocol` is absent or 1, every response must be byte-identical to today INCLUDING the absence of any new field: NO `protocolVersion` key may appear in a start response unless the caller requested version >= 2. Emission is conditional on the session's negotiated protocol, never unconditional. Rewrite planned test T1: a no-protocol start must assert the raw serialized response JSON does NOT contain the substring "protocolVersion"; a companion test asserts a protocol:2 start returns protocolVersion === 2 in the raw JSON. The reviewed plan's `const protocolVersion = protocol ?? 1;` included unconditionally in the returned object is REJECTED.

R3 (output schema representation; resolves CF5 + VF7b, consistent with R2). StartToolOutputSchema gains `protocolVersion: z.number().int().min(1).max(2).optional()`. The `.max(2)` matches the input bound (CF5). `.optional()` and NOT `.default(1)`: z.default makes the field required in the schema's inferred output type, and buildResponse (start.ts:157-253) returns a plain object typed StartToolOutput with no .parse round-trip, so `.default(1)` would force unconditional emission and re-create the R2 violation (or require a cast). Consumers derive v1 semantics as `parsed.protocolVersion ?? 1`. This additive-optional shape is also what T-033 may later export; do not loosen `.strict()`.

R4 (protocol field placement; resolves CF3 + VF7a). `protocol` must NOT be added to sharedStartShape (src/schema/params.ts:19-33): that shape is spread into StartParamsSchema (params.ts:42-56), and adding it there leaks a wire-negotiation field into the StartParams domain type and the prompt-building input. Instead add `protocol: z.number().int().min(1).max(2).default(1)` to the two arms of StartToolInputSchema only (src/tools/start.ts:57-74). In buildResponse, destructure `protocol` out alongside lensConfig/preambleConfig/projectContext BEFORE startParamsLike is formed (keeps promptHashes and lens-cache keys stable) and pass it to registerReview as a separate param. Unknown or higher values REJECT at the input boundary via `.max(2)`; do not clamp or coerce (the reviewed plan's word "clamps" is wrong; VF7a). Also add `protocol: { type: "integer", minimum: 1, maximum: 2 }` to the listTools inputSchema hint (start.ts:120-129) and mention negotiation in the tool description.

R5 (persistence; ratifies plan edits 3-4 with one amendment). ReviewSession gains `readonly protocolVersion: number`; registerReview gains `protocol?: number` and stores `params.protocol ?? 1`; persistRegistrationBestEffort writes it into the IndexRecord; hydrateFromDisk restores `index.protocolVersion ?? 1`. Amendment: IndexRecordSchema (src/cache/in-flight.ts:99-129) uses `z.number().int().min(1).max(2).optional()` (add the `.max(2)`, symmetric with R3). Absence means v1; CURRENT_IN_FLIGHT_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 (purely additive, pre-existing on-disk records still parse under .strict()). Restart test T8 (protocol survives `_clearMapOnlyForTests` via index rehydration) is mandatory.

R6 (v2 retry transport, the core deliverable; ratifies plan edits 5-7). NextActionSchema (src/schema/review-protocol.ts:90-98, today .strict() with required retryPrompt) becomes: `retryPrompt` optional, new `retryContext` optional, plus a superRefine requiring EXACTLY ONE of the two present (planned test T7 mandatory; the schema's only in-repo usages, verdict.ts:83 and the public-api retryPrompt-only literal, stay green). buildNextActions defines the retry suffix ONCE; the v1 branch emits `retryPrompt = prompt + suffix` byte-identical to today's string at complete.ts:273; the v2 branch emits `retryContext = suffix` and no retryPrompt. Binding invariant, pinned by mandatory test T5: basePrompt (via lens_review_get_prompt) + retryContext === v1 retryPrompt, byte-for-byte. Keep the `if (prompt === undefined) continue` guard in both branches. Update lensReviewCompleteDefinition.description and the get-prompt doc comment (get-prompt.ts:24-29): under v2 the agent re-fetches the BASE prompt and appends retryContext client-side; get_prompt still NEVER returns a retry prompt, so the existing invariant is extended, not violated.

R7 (no v2-only truncation; resolves VF7c). Do NOT truncate the failure reason inside v2 retryContext. A v2-only cap would break R6's byte-equality invariant, which is the mechanism behind acceptance bullet 5 (identical verdicts). Unbounded Zod reason summaries are a pre-existing v1 characteristic, not a regression introduced here. Planned test T3 keeps its `retryContext.length < 1024` assertion by using a fixture with a controlled short parse-failure reason (the existing parse-failure fixture pattern near test/tools-complete.test.ts:158), and additionally asserts the retryContext does not contain the artifact sentinel. Document the unbounded-reason characteristic in a code comment. If a cap is ever wanted, it must be applied to v1 and v2 identically in one change, not here.

R8 (hop-1 budget pin; resolves VF3). ACCEPTANCE bullet 1 requires an explicit test even though the property already holds at HEAD via T-022. Extend planned test T2: start with protocol: 2 and a large artifact (>100KB) containing a sentinel string; assert `JSON.stringify(response).length < 5120` and that the serialized response does not contain the sentinel, while `get_prompt(reviewId, lensId)` DOES contain it.

R9 (direct verdict-equivalence test; resolves VF4). ACCEPTANCE bullet 5 says "Test:", so transitive coverage via T5 is insufficient. Add a direct end-to-end test: run identical lens submissions through one protocol-1 review and one protocol-2 review over the same inputs; assert equal verdict, severity counts, and findings (modulo reviewId/sessionId and the nextActions payload shape). This also guards against future protocol-conditional drift in the merger path.

R10 (baseline + gates; resolves VF1 + CF4). The plan's "Baseline 575/575" is stale: at 770cfd5, npm test is 599/599 in 27 files (re-run and confirmed during this adjudication). Binding process rule: re-derive the suite count at the ACTUAL parent commit at plan time (T-026, and possibly T-027, will have moved it again); never carry a count forward from an older spec. Required pre-commit gates: `npm test` AND `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit, package.json:23); `npm run build` is recommended since the package publishes generated declarations. The tools-complete EEXIST stderr is documented failure-injection noise; those tests pass.

R11 (T-026/T-027 sequencing and expiry-surface re-anchor; resolves VF5 and the T-032 side of T-027's REVIEW_EXPIRED wording desync). T-032 must NOT run concurrently with T-026 or T-027; serialize behind whichever of them lands, and rebase all citations. T-027 (same wave, 1.5.0 critical path) rewrites the exact surfaces T-032 touches: the hop-1 expiry reuse inside buildNextActions (complete.ts:270-272 region) and the whole-call review_expired rejection (review-state.ts:445-454) become per-lens acceptance with terminal expired coverage. Therefore: (a) planned test T6 must pin the expiry semantics AS THEY EXIST at T-032's parent commit; if T-027 has landed, a past-TTL later hop surfaces through the post-T-027 typed expiry surface (per-lens expired coverage / PARTIAL_RESULTS or the retained whole-review TTL error), not necessarily today's whole-call REVIEW_EXPIRED shape, and SCOPE-4's "typed REVIEW_EXPIRED" is to be read as "the typed expiry surface as it exists post-T-027"; annotate T6 accordingly. (b) T-032 must not remove, rename, or reword the REVIEW_EXPIRED error code or LENS_ERROR_MESSAGES entry on its own; the code stays a produced surface for later hops against reviews past the 24h in-flight TTL (DEFAULT_TTL_MS, in-flight.ts:51), and message wording is owned by T-027's adjudicated edit (neutral wording, no "no longer produced" claim).

R12 (scope fences with the explicit descope record CF1 demanded). The hop-1 `artifact | artifactRef` INPUT option in SCOPE-1 is OUT of T-032 even under Option A: T-026 retains the artifact per-review (keyed by reviewId) and defines no cross-review artifactRef input; no consumer needs one today (verified: no workspace code couples to the lenses wire format). If a consumer materializes, file a new ticket. T-032's deliverable set is exactly: tool-boundary protocol negotiation (R4), conditional protocolVersion echo (R2/R3), persistence (R5), v2 compact retryContext with byte-equality invariant (R6/R7), and tests T1-T8 as amended plus R8/R9. No changes to merger, verdict computation, dedup, tension, lens prompt bodies, or get_prompt behavior. The T-030 centralized-floor design is untouched by this ticket.
title: reviewId-keyed delta protocol -- stop re-shipping the artifact and full prompts after hop-1
